extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, editors, and publishers of medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: The ICMJE Recommendations provide formal guidance on the conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals, covering authorship, conflicts of interest, peer review, trial registration, manuscript preparation, corrections/retractions, and related editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the aims and scope of the Recommendations for conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index page lists this section title; full explanatory guidance is in the Recommendations document (PDF/web).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Should Use the Recommendations?
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies the intended users of the Recommendations (e.g., authors, editors, peer reviewers, publishers, institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title present on page; consult full text for detailed audience-specific advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: History of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Background and evolution of the ICMJE Recommendations and their rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as context/background material; no substantive criteria on index page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles & Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the responsibilities of parties involved in scholarly publishing (authors, editors, peer reviewers, publishers, institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section header only here; full Recommendations contain specific duties and expectations for each role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining the Role of Authors and Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for who qualifies as an author versus contributor and how contributions should be reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index lists the heading; detailed authorship criteria (e.g., contribution, accountability) are in the main document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Responsibilities—Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for authors to disclose financial and non-financial conflicts of interest and how to report them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading appears on page; full disclosure standards and examples are in the Recommendations and disclosure forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities in the Submission and Peer-Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and expectations for submitting manuscripts and for the conduct of peer reviewers and editors during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index header only; full guidance covers ethical submission practices, reviewer confidentiality, timeliness, and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Owners and Editorial Freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles protecting editorial independence from journal owners, sponsors, or advertisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a topic; full text contains policies to safeguard editorial decisions and handle undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Research Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for protecting human (and animal) subjects, including ethical approval, informed consent, and reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title present; detailed requirements (ethics committee approval, consent statements) are in the Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing & Editorial Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: General policies on editorial processes, publication decisions, and related operational issues for journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad heading on index; full guidance addresses processes such as handling submissions, corrections, and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and Version Control
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for issuing corrections, errata, and managing different versions of published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading appears on page; detailed procedures for correction notices, linking, and version history are in the Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Misconduct, Expressions of Concern, and Retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for identifying and responding to suspected misconduct, issuing expressions of concern, and retracting papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed topic; full document gives recommended investigation steps, notice formats, and criteria for retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on copyright ownership, licensing, and rights transfer between authors and journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title only here; full Recommendations explain copyright transfer, open access licenses, and related practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies regarding duplicate publication, redundant publication, and acceptable reuse (e.g., preprints, secondary analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a topic; detailed definitions and handling procedures are in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for publishing letters, correspondence, responses, and how journals should handle them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading present; full guidance includes length limits, disclosure expectations, and editorial treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements, Theme Issues, and Special Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for publishing supplements, themed issues, and sponsored series, including transparency about sponsorship and editorial control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entry only; full Recommendations detail disclosure and editorial independence expectations for supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship or Partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for disclosing and managing relationships with sponsors or partners involved in the research or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading is listed; full guidance addresses financial support disclosure and sponsor influence on content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance specific to online publication platforms, digital archiving, and electronic dissemination practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic appears on page; full Recommendations cover technical and policy considerations for electronic publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing advertising in journals and its separation from editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title only here; full text defines acceptable advertising practices and firewalling editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals and the Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on interactions between journals, authors, and the media, including press releases and embargoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a topic; detailed recommendations on media relations are in the main document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that clinical trials be registered in a public registry before patient enrollment and reporting policies for trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears on the index; the ICMJE requires prospective registration and specifies acceptable registries—details are in the Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and instructions for preparing manuscripts for submission (formatting, structure, reporting standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading present; full Recommendations include specific requirements (e.g., CONSORT for trials) and formatting advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing for Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical steps and checks authors should complete before submitting a manuscript (e.g., disclosures, approvals, formatting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed topic; the full text provides checklists and required statements for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending the Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and expectations for the act of submitting manuscripts, including cover letters, submission systems, and declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading only on index; the Recommendations describe required submission materials and declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for publishing translated material and handling non-English versions of articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed topic; full guidance covers acknowledgment of original publication and permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archives
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on archiving published content for long-term preservation and access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title present; detailed archiving best practices are in the Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall framework for how journals should manage and disclose conflicts of interest among authors, reviewers, and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears multiple times in the index; full Recommendations and accompanying disclosure forms provide specific policies and templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest Disclosure Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized forms and procedures for collecting conflict of interest disclosures from authors and contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed as a resource; the page links to the ICMJE disclosure form used by many journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Following the ICMJE Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for journals and stakeholders on adopting and implementing the ICMJE Recommendations in policy and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section header present; details include how journals should state adherence and implement specific policies.
